title: Homestretch shift handoff - raw journal
content:
TL;DR
- Quietish shift; one recurring memory spike on quantized-gpu nodes (see incident note below).
- Applied temporary throttle on long-polling embedder requests; needs follow-up to root cause.
- No customer-facing outages; one ephemeral degraded tail latency for chat streaming (p95 -> 1.1s to 1.6s for ~20m at 02:10 UTC).

Shift summary (chronological)
- 21:05 UTC: Took over from Rhea. Quick scan: infra dashboards green, error budget for hosted-api routes in low-risk zone.
- 22:18 UTC: Alert: node quant-gpu-07 high memory (OOM throttle on inference-worker). Prometheus spike correlates with long-running embed requests from /v1/embeddings (client: sandbox-team).
  * Action: scale down batch_size for that route via feature-gate (temporary) and added 60s prefix cache TTL. Patch applied: feature-gate/embeddings-throttle=on.
  * Result: Mem stabilized after 8m.
- 02:10 UTC: Short (20m) tail-latency blip on streaming chat route, traced to one overloaded router pod. Did a live restart (kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-router -n redwood-serving). Pod came back in 35s and p95 returned to normal.
- 03:40 UTC: Noticed repeated redis slowlog entries (~5ms -> 70ms) when background cache-repopulate job runs. Disabled job schedule temporarily (cronjob/cache-repopulate) and filed INF-2301.

Incident: quant-gpu-07 memory spikes (recurring)
- Symptoms: sudden RSS increase on inference-worker container, resulting in OOMKills. Pods on same node show high /sys/fs/cgroup memory pressure.
- Temporary mitigation performed: enabled embeddings throttle + reduced batch_size on the sandbox route, restarted affected pod.
- Immediate TODO: confirm whether KV cache (local) is evicting incorrectly and causing re-populate thrash. Watch for frequent GC logs in container stdout.
- Follow-ups: SRE ticket (SRE-4127) assigned to Marcus. Recommend: repro with same request pattern in staging and enable heavy-metrics capture (jemalloc stats, nvml snapshots).

Quick checks to run on handoff (do these first)
1) infra status: curl -s http://status.redwood.internal/health || echo "status page not reachable"
2) k8s: kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving -o wide | egrep "CrashLoop|OOM|NotReady"
3) recent alerts: grafana -> alert history (filter: last 6h)
4) expensive routes: check /v1/embeddings and /v1/generate tail latency dashboards
5) redis: redis-cli -h redis.master info | egrep "used_memory|latency"

Useful commands / snippets (copyable)
- Restart router deployment: kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-router -n redwood-serving
- Scale embeddings workers: kubectl scale deploy/embeddings-workers --replicas=2 -n redwood-serving
- Tail logs for suspect pod: kubectl logs -f pod/inference-worker-abc -n redwood-serving --timestamps --since=10m
- Check GPU memory via node-exporter metrics in Grafana: node_namespace_pod_container:container_memory_rss_bytes{container=~"inference-worker.*"}

Known workarounds (temporary)
- embeddings: feature-gate throttle (feature-gate/embeddings-throttle=on) - reduces batch_size and enforces 200ms max batch window. Not permanent.
- cache-repopulate job: moved from 03:30 -> manual trigger to avoid peak redis latency.

Open questions / unresolved
- Why does quantized model path trigger heavy host memory pressure despite smaller model size? Hypothesis: jemalloc fragmentation + KV cache rehydration loop. Need to capture jemalloc stats during spike.
- Is there a client pattern (sandbox-team) repeatedly sending huge input arrays to embeddings? Marcus to ask them for examples.
- Should we add an alert for jemalloc allocated > 70% for >3m on inference-worker containers?

Handoff checklist (what I did / what you should do)
- Done: Added temporary throttle on sandbox embeddings route, disabled cache-repopulate cronjob, restarted router pod when streaming blip occurred.
- To do: 1) Re-enable cronjob only after redis SLAs are validated in staging. 2) Run repro load against quant-gpu channel in staging (ticket SRE-4127). 3) If spike persists, evacuate node and cordon if necessary (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets).

Escalation contacts (order)
- Primary SRE: Marcus Green (pager)
- Secondary infra eng: Rhea Patel (slack oncall)
- Platform eng: Priya Nair (email + pager)
- CEO/Critical comms: ops@redwood.com (only for customer-impacting incidents)

Notes to next shift
- Watch for repeated memory spikes on quant nodes between 22:00-04:00 UTC window — pattern seen 3 times in last week.
- If you see the sandbox client pattern, temporarily block via WAF rule and notify sandbox team.
- Add a short entry in SRE-4127 with exact timestamps and pod names if you perform any additional restarts. Saves Marcus time.

Loose ideas (brainstorm)
- Consider per-model jemalloc arenas tuning for quantized paths. Might help fragmentation.
- Add a lightweight synthetic workload that exercises KV cache rehydration in staging during quiet hours.

Misc small TODOs (personal)
- Write up short runbook snippet for embeddings throttle (2-3 steps) and commit to docs.
- Add alert for redis slowlog > 50ms over 2m.

Final: leaving the cluster at 04:30 UTC, everything stabilized but not resolved. Please ping me (liam.chen@redwood.com) if you need context or if something flares up.

-- Liam
